gañja (EI 30), Persian ganj; a treasury or store-house. Utpala on the Bṛhatsaṃhitā, 52. 13, explains gañja as kośa-bhavana, i. e. treasury. See Gañjavara.
 (IE 8-8), a store-house of liquor.
Gañj-ādhikārin (HRS), a treasury-officer according to the Rājataraṅgiṇī. See Gañjapati, etc.
Gañjapati (EI 13; HRS; HD), same as Persian Ganjwar, treasurer (Ep. Ind., Vol. XIII, p. 115). See gañja.
